rejected.title: Technology that drives discovery
card: New technology lets scientists collect data that was impossible to gather before. Better data can lead to new questions and new discoveries.
Radio telescopes

These collect faint radio waves given off by objects in space, such as galaxies. Our eyes cannot see radio waves. They do not send signals out. The Australian SKA Pathfinder in Western Australia is one, and it can survey large areas of sky.
DNA sequencing machines
These read the order of the bases that make up DNA, without changing them. They let scientists compare the genes of many living things quickly.
The tool does not reach conclusions by itself. Scientists analyse the new data it collects, and that analysis drives discovery.
rejected.remember: New tools collect data that scientists could not gather before, and analysing that data leads to discoveries.

a.q: Why can a radio telescope such as ASKAP reveal objects in space that our eyes miss?
opts: It collects faint radio waves given off by objects
It sends out radio waves and times their echoes
It magnifies visible light more than other telescopes
It detects ultraviolet light that our eyes cannot see
a.why: Objects such as galaxies give off radio waves, which our eyes cannot see, and a radio telescope collects them. It does not send signals out and time echoes, which is how radar works.
a.clue: Does the telescope send anything, or only receive?

b.q: A team uses DNA sequencing to read genes from hundreds of frog species in one month. How does this help drive discovery?
opts: Scientists can analyse far more data to test new ideas
The machine works out which species are most related
The machine changes the bases so genes match more easily
The machine shows each frog's whole body in fine detail
b.why: The machine reads the order of bases quickly, giving scientists far more data to analyse. It does not reach conclusions such as which species are related: scientists do that by analysing the data.
b.clue: Who draws conclusions, the machine or the scientists?

draft.title: Technology that drives discovery
card: New technology lets scientists collect data that was impossible to gather before. Better data can lead to new questions and new discoveries.
Radio telescopes
These detect radio waves from space, which our eyes cannot see. The Australian SKA Pathfinder in Western Australia is one example, and it can survey large areas of sky.
DNA sequencing machines
These read the order of the bases that make up DNA. They let scientists compare the genes of many living things quickly.
Each tool extends what scientists can observe or measure. It is the new data from the tool that drives discovery.
draft.remember: New tools collect data that scientists could not gather before, and that data leads to discoveries.

a.q: How does a radio telescope help scientists discover new things about space?
opts: It detects radio waves that our eyes cannot see
It lets scientists travel to distant stars
It makes distant objects switch on radio signals
It replaces the need to collect any data
a.why: Radio waves carry information about objects in space, and a radio telescope can detect them. It does not move scientists anywhere, and it still produces data that must be studied.
a.clue: Think about what light our eyes cannot detect.

b.q: Before DNA sequencing machines, comparing the genes of two species took years. Now it can take days. What is the main effect on research?
opts: Scientists can gather and compare far more genetic data
Scientists no longer need to ask any questions
Genes of different species have become more similar
Scientists can now see DNA with the naked eye
b.why: Faster sequencing gives scientists much more data to compare, which can lead to new questions. The machines read DNA but do not change it, and they do not remove the need for questions.
b.clue: Ask what the machine changes about the data collected.

a.best: It detects radio waves that our eyes cannot see

b.best: Scientists can gather and compare far more genetic data

a.q: How can ASKAP detect objects in space that are invisible to our eyes?
opts: It collects faint radio waves that the objects give off
It sends out radio waves and times the returning echoes
It magnifies visible light more than other telescopes
It picks up ultraviolet light that our eyes cannot see
a.why: Objects such as galaxies give off radio waves, which our eyes cannot see, and ASKAP collects them. It does not send signals out and time their echoes, which is how radar works.
